architectural_determination: The certified productive gap is real but only a narrow general policy change is justified by the evidence. ROBY may recommend the sole survivor of explicit required constraints while keeping unknown non-required evidence visible. The first six H6 cases do not justify a broader incomplete-evidence dominance heuristic.

contract_rules.R1: An explicitly unfavorable required criterion continues to BLOCK an option.
contract_rules.R2: Missing evidence is not negative evidence and must never be converted to UNFAVORABLE.
contract_rules.R3: Missing evidence on non-required criteria normally remains INSUFFICIENT and preserves epistemic uncertainty.
contract_rules.R4: A recommendation may be emitted when exactly one option survives all explicit required criteria and every competing option is BLOCKED by at least one explicit required criterion.
contract_rules.R5: Under R4, missing evidence on non-required criteria may not veto the sole required-criterion survivor, but must remain visible in rationale/tradeoff evidence.
contract_rules.R6: No recommendation is authorized merely because one option has more favorable observations when criterion importance or complete comparative evidence is absent.
contract_rules.R7: Explicit importance relations may support a future general dominance rule only under a separate contract; they are not part of this change.
contract_rules.R8: The change must live in the existing governed complex-decision authority; no benchmark router, adapter rule or parallel decision authority is permitted.

hcpdq_case_disposition.V2E-H6-001_to_006: NO_CHANGE_AUTHORIZED_FROM_THIS_RESULT; current prompts do not express a required criterion or frozen importance relation sufficient for a principled recommendation under incomplete evidence.
hcpdq_case_disposition.V2E-H6-007_to_012: IN_SCOPE; each prompt explicitly marks one criterion required, one option fails it, and the competing option satisfies it.
